item.title: l.e.g.o. Box TB Hotel – Geocache of the week
item.description:
Traditional
GC86BFD
by FLF
Difficulty:
2
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Germany
N 49° 18.623 E 007° 16.962

Some geocaches are clever. Others are beautiful. And then there are those that make you feel like you’ve discovered a secret hiding place built purely for joy. L.E.G.O. Box TB Hotel (GC86BFD) is exactly that kind of cache.

Your adventure begins behind a curtain of green leaves. What looks like a simple, overgrown entrance quickly turns into a hidden nook, where something playful and unexpected awaits. The approach alone feels like a quiet invitation to step into a miniature world.

Once you reach the cache, the fist challenge presents itself: a lock. To open it, you’ll need to crack a light puzzle by taking the letter values from the alphabet of “LEGO” and calculating the digit sum of each letter. The result gives you the code for Lock 1—a neat, thematic puzzle that sets the tone for what’s to come.

Inside, you’re greeted by a beautifully built LEGO® house. This isn’t just a container; it’s an interactive creation designed with care and precision by FLF (Felix and Freya). Inside the door, clear instructions guide you through the process.

Following these steps feels a bit like operating a tiny LEGO machine. Begin by pumping on the left side of the box. Then move the switch upward, and the drawer will slide open. Inside, you’ll find the cache container with the code for lock 2—after obtaining the code, carefully place it back where it belongs.

Next, pump a few more times, then move the switch downward to allow the drawer to slide back in. Set the switch to the middle position, close the wooden box, and secure it with Lock 1.

A gentle reminder from the cache owner, FLF:

please don’t pull or push the drawer by hand. The mechanism is designed to do the work for you.”

But the experience doesn’t end there. Hidden inside the pole of the LEGO house is another surprise, secured with lock 2. Opening it reveals a LEGO Travel Bug hotel, a playful and secure stop for trackables before they continue their journey.

The cache owner, FLF, thoughtfully planned for all seasons. When temperatures drop too low, and the technology doesn’t cooperate, a winter edition comes into play, confirming that visitors can still log their find, using a backup or SOS logbook.

As with any cache on private property, respect is essential. Visitors are asked not to block the driveway and to park on the street, ensuring this joyful hide can remain available for future seekers.

L.E.G.O. Box TB Hotel captures the spirit of geocaching at its most fun. It invites you to slow down, explore, and enjoy every step of the process. Between the hidden entrance and the clever LEGO mechanics, it’s clear this cache was designed to bring a smile.

Have you ever found a cache that felt less like a container and more like a small moment of magic?

Header image by Sébal_Family.

item.title: Start your next hide with the coordinate collector in the Geocaching® app
item.description:
Hiding a geocache just got easier!

With the new coordinate collector in the Geocaching® app (version 10.2.0+ on iOS and version 10.3.0+ on Android), you can collect and name coordinates right in the app. The feature is available now on iOS and will roll out on Android shortly. If you’re on Android and don’t see it yet, it will appear once version 10.3.0 is available to you.

Your saved coordinates automatically sync to your cache owner dashboard on Geocaching.com.

No more screenshots, additional waypoints, or wondering why you saved a location. Just open the Hides tab in the app to access the coordinate collector and get started.

With coordinate collector, you can:

  • Collect and name coordinates: Save locations in the app and give each one a custom name, like “By the big pine tree.”
  • Gauge GPS accuracy: The app does the work for you—when you tap Collect coordinates, it filters out poor readings and averages multiple signals to give you a more reliable result.
  • Access your saved coordinates on Geocaching.com: Your coordinates appear on your cache owner dashboard, ready to use when you create a cache page.

This is just the first step toward a more mobile-friendly hiding experience, with more updates coming soon.

NOTE: Saving coordinates does not reserve or guarantee a location for your cache. To learn more about hiding guidelines, visit the Help Center.

item.title: The Matterhorn — Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GC8DJV4
by geocachingvlogger
Difficulty:
2.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Minnesota, United States
N 44° 44.024′ W 093° 13.341′

🏔️ This takes geocaching to new heights! 🏔️

A gadget cache to lift the spirits without letting your feet leave the groundis a must for every geocacher! Look no further than this clever geocache in a quiet shopping center in Minnesota.

Placed with permission back in the summer of 2019, this geocache has produced over 200 Favorite points and was cleverly created by geocachingvlogger. This Geocache of the Week requires a tool that geocachers must bring with them before attempting to reach the summit and make the find: two 5/16-inch (0.7 cm) dowels, each around a foot long.

Once at the posted coordinates with the required tools, it’s time to open the cache and sign the logbook… but how?

Study the structure and notice the small holes on the sides. They are just the right size for the dowels brought along on the adventure. The puck inside the gadget must reach the top of the mountain to reveal the code and, ultimately, the logbook.


Video by truitt_johnson.

Serious coordination, patience, and perseverance are required to claim this smiley. Once geocachers have maneuvered the puck to the top and revealed the code, it’s time to open the locked compartment and sign the log sheet!

Note: Please do not insert anything into the cache that could break off or scratch its inside.

What geocache took you to new heights? Share them with us in the comments below!

There are six available souvenirs for the following milestones:

  • Collecting 200 Treasures

item.title: A seasonal tradition: Holiday & winter geocache trails
item.description:
Geocachers celebrate the holidays in many ways—from earning souvenirs and hosting Events to finding “just one more cache” before the year ends. In many places, a popular tradition is holiday and winter geocache trails.

Throughout fall and winter, local geocachers create seasonal series to give back to the community. Some trails release one cache per day like an advent calendar, while others publish all at once for a planned outing. No matter the format, they share the same spirit: creativity, generosity, and community.

Check out some winter geocache series from around the world:

A Team Effort in British Columbia—Advent 25 (BMF5J2V)
Not all holiday trails are solo projects. This series is shared among three cache owners, turning it into a collaborative gift for the community. Collaborative trails can be a fun way to distribute planning, creativity, and maintenance, while also building community connections.

An Annual Tradition—Adventskalender SG 2025 (BMF5J3F)
For some geocachers, Advent trails are an annual tradition. The German geocaching team KlingenXmasCommunity publishes an Advent trail year after year, creating something local geocachers look forward to each holiday season. Twenty-four Mystery Caches challenge geocachers to solve Christmas-themed riddles to find a festive surprise.

A Long-Running Series in Norway—VV Advent Cache Series (BMF65K1)
This winter Advent series in Norway shows how holiday trails are a lasting community tradition. Published in 2023 and still active, it’s a great example of an Advent-style series that continues to bring geocachers outside long after the season ends. The geocaching community Vestfold Vikings in Vestfold released an Advent series every year for many years.

Winter Makes the Route Possible (Alaska)—Winter Series (BMF5J41)
In Alaska, winter doesn’t just add atmosphere; it can change the landscape. This winter series turns a difficult summer route into a winter-friendly geocaching experience.

5 Hints to Winter Caching in Minnesota Series (BMF5J46)
This winter cache series in Minnesota aims to educate geocachers on winter safety. Each geocache in the series provides useful tips and tricks for enjoying geocaching safely and responsibly in the winter!

Feeling inspired? Here are some suggestions for designing your own seasonal geocache series:

Winter cache trails are meant to be fun, festive, and community-focused, but they can come with extra challenges.

Here are a few tips and reminders for cache owners and seekers to help keep the experience safe and enjoyable:

  • Winter isn’t just a season; it’s a setting. In many parts of the world, accessing the cache changes with the season. Frozen creeks, packed snow trails, and seasonal routes can make a cache easier or harder to find.
  • Use clear attributes and seasonal warnings. If a cache depends on frozen conditions, make it clear on the cache page. If travel routes, parking, and accessibility change based on the season, include those details so geocachers can plan accordingly.
  • Consider longevity. Geocaches are intended to last for at least three months. Design your hides and trails to be enjoyed by the community beyond a single season.
  • Plan for winter conditions. Shorter daylight hours, weather, and trail conditions matter; always read the cache description, review attributes, and follow local safety guidance. For winter hides, seekers should always use judgment and safe practices.

Do you have a winter caching tradition in your community, such as winter trails, annual events, themed hides, or a favorite “first find of the year” ritual?

We’d love to hear about it. Share your favorite seasonal series, winter-friendly hides, or end-of-year geocaching traditions, and let’s inspire one another, no matter which hemisphere you’re caching in.

Happy caching, and Happy New Year!

item.title: ON 12.22 : Roermond – Remunj — Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GCBDAF8
by nicoletje
Difficulty:
2
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Limburg, Netherlands
N 51° 10.902’ E 006° 00.638’

As we tie our shoes and boot up our GPSs for a new year of adventures, we bring you more geocaches every week that embody the “wow” factor.

This week, we spotlight ON 12.22 : Roermond – Remunj (GCBDAF8), a cleverly crafted traditional hide tucked into a welcoming residential corner of Roermond, Netherlands, and is both a local charm and a geocaching engineering marvel.

As you arrive at Ground Zero (GZ), you’re greeted by the town’s distinctive charm, setting the stage for the search ahead. Patience is essential here, as the cache page makes it clear this is far from a quick grab-and-go.

After an initial search, you may feel tempted to use the hint on the cache page, which suggests there is mail for you. The only logical object in proximity is a red mailbox. The mailbox opens when you enter the correct combination into its protective lock.

Inside, you’ll find instructions on how to find and unlock the highly anticipated cache. As the details unfold, it soon becomes evident that the nearby well is no coincidence, but the focal point of the search.

Upon unlocking the well and its hoisting mechanism, you come face-to-face with a striking octagon-shaped barrel container, standing proudly in your path. Use the hoisting mechanism to lift the container and gain access to the geocache.

Video by hebbes_geocachingvideo.

Open the container, and you’ll be awestruck by a diorama depicting a house with different rooms. While each room is quirky in its own way, the common thread is wandering cats making themselves right at home.

Once you’ve spent some time looking at each detail, you’ll find the cache, along with some SWAG, trackables, and the log sheet, carefully tucked into one side.

The cache is listed as owned by both Ommetje_Nederland and nicoletje—a team effort! The cache has already received 55 Favorite points since its publication in December of 2025, and overwhelmingly positive logs.

The cache owners share that countless hours of dedication went into creating this experience. Seekers are encouraged to approach the cache thoughtfully and handle it with care.

Header image by PartickRoger.

As we begin 2026, we invite geocachers to bring their creative energy into the new year. Each hidden geocache creates an adventure and makes each finder an explorer.

Hidden in plain sight—urban edition 🫣

item.title: Danke Prora 2013 – Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GC47NWY
by ruegenspass.eu
Difficulty:
2.5
Terrain:
2
Location:
Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany
N 54° 27.134 E 013° 34.276

We’re kicking off our 2026 Geocache of the Week series with a twist, quite literally!

History, craftsmanship, and geocaching are spun together at Danke Prora 2013 (GC47NWY).


As its name suggests, Danke Prora 2013 (GC47NWY) has been turning heads since its debut in 2013, created to honor the first-ever Mega Event (GC44477) at Prora on the island of Rügen, Germany. And what a fitting location for a large Event; the massive Colossus of Prora stretches nearly 3 miles (4.5 kilometers) along the shoreline. Built during World War II but never completed, the largely empty structure remains a stark reminder of its past and provides a memorable setting for this geocache.

Just outside sits an ordinary metal sign with an emblem depicting Rügen’s rugged outline. But this sign is more than meets the eye; It’s a geocache in disguise! Read the cache page carefully to discover this cache’s secrets. With a simple twist, the emblem opens to reveal a hidden compartment, and inside it, the geocache container.

The cache owner, ruegenspass.eu, a professional metalworker and construction manager, designed and built the cache by hand. Like all of his creations, it began as an idea, took shape on paper, and was then carefully brought to life with the help of his wife, Grit.

For ruegenspass.eu and Grit, geocaching is about more than finding caches. They love exploring remarkable locations across different countries, meeting kind and interesting people, and creating caches that bring joy to others.

When the Mega Event organizing team asked them to design a special cache for the Event, they saw it as an opportunity to give something back to the community. The cache was published as a heartfelt thank you, and every detail reflects their goal of making each cache unique, engaging, and fun to find.

item.title: We asked you: what are your geocaching goals for 2026?
item.description:
A new year is a natural moment to pause, reflect, and look ahead. In geocaching, that can mean setting a clear goal—or simply staying open to wherever the game leads next.

Some geocachers start the year with a plan, like completing a challenge, exploring new places, or focusing on a favorite cache type or difficulty. Others take a more flexible approach, fitting geocaching into everyday life and using it as a way to get outside and connect with their community.

We asked geocachers to share what they’ve set out to accomplish in 2026.

Note: some of the responses have been edited for clarity and brevity.

“Get my 5,000th find and find a cache in Quebec to earn the Quebec souvenir.” – Kevin C.

“We are planning to do a lap of Australia in our van, hoping to explore and find lots of caches in some small Aussie outback towns.” – Kitty H.

“Organizing my first Mega-Event (GCB89NQ) with friends in France next May! Signal the Frog® will be present—hope to see you all there as well!” – Arnokovic

“Hide a geocache on Rurutu in the Austral Islands of French Polynesia.” – Damien V.

“Make more geocaching friends that I can meet up with in person! Also, I want to get to 1000 finds. I started in September and am currently at about 350.” – Angela C.

“My goal? To find lots more caches!” – Leah M.

“If all goes to plan, I’ll be attending my first Mega-Event, Bamarama (GCB2R1R), in 2026!” – David L.

“To hide my own caches” – Gina C.

“I want to get a few more EarthCaches published and finish the counties in Michigan this coming summer. I hope to attend Yuma again and maybe GeoWoodstock in Kansas in May. I also want to have fun, explore more, and meet more geocachers.” – Terri Y

“1. Go geocaching. 2. Go geocaching. 3. Go geocaching.” – Elijah S.

What are your 2026 geocaching goals? Share your answer in the comments below!

item.title: Top 10 Geocaches of the Week 2025
item.description:
This year was exceptional for unique geocaches worldwide, and we’ve compiled a list of the top 10 to share. From a clever disguise in Switzerland and a colorful gadget cache in Texas to a not-so-little library in Canada and a sneaky lock near an iconic Spanish landmark, the variety is sure to excite.

To create this list, we evaluated the most-liked geocaches on our blog, Facebook, and YouTube. Each week, we spotlight diverse geocaches from around the globe. Now, we want to hear your favorites!

1.) Remember Depot Wiesenplatz – GC7PNK0


Video by giacaches.

Hidden in an unexpected location below the surface is a well-camouflaged geocache with more than 150 Favorite points. In downtown Klybeck, one sewer grate is home to a geocache that attracts the community.

Thousands of pedestrians walk past this spot, unaware that a world-famous geocache is hidden right below their feet. Visit the sidewalk in Klybeck, Switzerland, to find this geocache (GC7PNK0).

2.) Bydir’s 10.000ste – GC6XWCC


Video by gc_anjoki.

Who doesn’t enjoy a relaxing geocache? This birdhouse container appears to be a quick find, but there’s more to discover. Join us at Bydir’s 10.000ste (GC6XWCC).

3.) You Make The Chain! ( Gadget Cache ) – GC6P20K


Video by geotabg.

Sometimes we encounter a complex gadget geocache and wonder how the cache owner created such a unique design.

This gadget cache asks geocachers to use the provided materials to make a tool, retrieve the key, and open the geocache (GC6P20K). The puzzle itself, however, is a real challenge.

4.) Harry Potters TB-Schloss – GC9ZD1Y


Video by northernblondeabroad.

Not far from nearby homes and the A13 highway is the TB castle of Harry Potter. This geocache (GC9ZD1Y) is located under the eaves of an unassuming building and is ready to be discovered. Finding the geocache is straightforward, but opening it requires geocachers to solve a code using a hint from the cache page.

5.) Motocyklová – GCAY4V9


Video by saulenite_geocaching.

What motivates you to geocache? Is it finding a new location, solving a puzzle, or hiking up a mountain?

In the streets of Prague, there is a geocache you won’t want to miss. Near the famous Kafka statue, you’ll find this geocache (GCAY4V9). While Prague has many spots for micro geocaches, this one is the size of a vehicle and stands out for its unique placement.

6.) Repeat After Me // Electronic Gadget Cache – GCB7ENP


Video by CacheCrikey.

Repeat after us: “I love geocaching,” “I love geocaching,” “I love geocaching!”

That was easy. Geocaching is fun for all experience levels. Multi-Cache (GCB7ENP) will test your memory and sense of adventure. Ready for a new challenge?

7.) Echoes Beyond the Gate – GCAWZTF


Video by GeoJudt.

Geocaching often reveals hidden parts of familiar places. Many geocachers discover new views or historic landmarks through geocaching.

Echoes Beyond the Gate (GCAWZTF) is a geocache hidden in a unique feature of the West Virginia Botanic Garden, a peaceful spot for wildlife and blooming flowers.

8.) Bridge Boutique – GCXCEX


Video by najmo_geocaching.

Near Toronto, there is a geocache known for its charm and unique design.

Hidden on Ward’s Island, Bridge Boutique (GCXCEX) features vibrant colors and creativity, reflecting the area’s community spirit.

9.) SAGRADA FAMÍLIA – GCA83B8


Video by mostly_moss.

Barcelona’s Sagrada Família is one of the world’s most celebrated architectural sites. Near Gaudí’s towers, a 3D-printed geocache (GCA83B8) is hidden for visitors to find.

This geocache reflects Gaudí’s spirit of innovation, and its 3D-printed lock combines technology and creativity in tribute to the architect and the basilica.

10.) Het Escapehouse – GCB4WBN


Video by creativecache.

Some geocaches test your navigation skills. Others challenge your puzzle-solving abilities. Het Escapehouse (GCB4WBN) combines both, inside a miniature replica of a real home.

Created by Nabuursjes with support from students at Praktijkschool De Singel and Arnoud van Uden, this geocache brings the escape room experience outdoors, complete with switches, clues, and a clever code.

item.title: A recap of our fourth 2025 hiding theme: Blast from the past! ⏳
item.description:
In 2025, we celebrated a major milestone—25 years of geocaching! To mark this special anniversary, we introduced a new hiding theme per quarter to celebrate geocaches published in 2025. Every three months, we featured geocaches from that quarter’s theme on the Geocaching Blog and social media.

For our fourth and final hiding theme of the year, each nomination helped us revisit memorable moments in geocaching. We struck retro gold with your ‘blast’tastic nominations and discovered caches that could make a highlight reel titled “geocaching’s greatest hits.”

Take a look at some caches that are time-capsule worthy:

  1. GCBC4JW—25 Jahre Geocaching
    Cache owner: Schtöffel 🇨🇭

Kicking things off strong with a mailbox celebrating 25 years of geocaching. Inside, you’ll find a quiz with 10 questions about the history of geocaching. If all questions are answered correctly, a door opens, revealing the logbook.

2. GCBDW2R—Blast from the Past of Gaming / ゲームの楽しい思い出
Cache owner: Tin999 🇯🇵

This creative multi-cache consists of four stages. At each stage, you will find an old game console that is reminiscent of childhood in the 90s. The posted coordinates for the next stage are on each console, and the last controller has the log sheet on its back.

3. GCAXATT—Jump (LFLs of Woodmoor)
Cache owner: whalesharklovas 🇺🇸

Part of a series focused on ’80s and ’90s hits, this gadget cache is based on the Van Halen mega-hit “Jump”, and cachers must encourage David Lee Roth to do his famous split leap to access the log sheet. As if all this Van Halen action wasn’t enough, the cache lives in the front yard of a Van Halen enthusiast, who encouraged the cache owner to think big.

4. GCBFTT4—Projection
Cache owner: alynx 🇨🇦

This cache container consists of an old slide projector. There are two cartridges, each holding 36 slides, that automatically feed the projector. The logbook is made of handmade slides that can be signed with Sharpies. This cache definitely brought us back to simpler times, even if just for a moment.

5. GC8XYTX—Hned zítra ráno zavolám
Cache owner: PA-ROF 🇨🇿

Did someone say cable salad? Dedicated to the 1975 Czech hit “I’ll Call You In The Morning” by Karel Gott, the cache container consists of a landline telephone. It might even confuse the younger generation of geocachers.

6. GC5BW5P—Kindheitserinnerungen III
Cache owner: Amöbenlimbo 🇩🇪

Celebrating its 11th birthday in August 2025, this cache features memorabilia that German kids growing up in the ‘70s and ‘80s will be very familiar with. Created with care and passion, you’ll find Bravo magazines, board games and toys, books, and many more classics from these decades.

7. GC8C348—A Photo Legacy
Cache owner: Quiltist2 🇺🇸

We’re bringing you major throwback vibes with this analog 35mm camera cache. The camera acts as the cache container, and inside you’ll find the log sheet wound on the film take-up spool.

8. GC8YH8F—Da liegt Musike drin…
Cache owner: Schnuffelbär64 🇩🇪

This cache is a smash hit! A puzzle requires geocachers to guess a Ricky King (German guitarist) song, which quickly transforms a charming geocaching bench into an instrumental concert! The final location reveals an authentic replica of an electric guitar—a true classic.

9. GCBEK9G—Dexter the Dino
Cache owner: HonuHideout 🇺🇸

Once upon a time, a dino named Dexter accidentally ate a log sheet—it is your mission to extract it. Find Dexter at your own discretion, though; you’ll have to tough out some thorns and rough terrain, graded a 4.

10. GCBEVTN—emotion
Cache owner: _nokos_ 🇯🇵

Video by geocaching_radio.

Do you ever get emotional looking at old polaroids or pictures from the days of disposable cameras? This cache owner is tapping into nostalgic vibes with this instant-print polaroid-style camera. Snap your picture, wait for it to print, and use it as your log sheet.

11. GCBB0DR—Balade au Thouars – LetterBox
Cache owner: YafaëL83 🇫🇷

We’ve spotted another 25 in the wild! This cache is located in Toulon in the Var region of France, and celebrates 25 years of geocaching and letterboxing, both of which originated in North America.

12. GCBFNVR—Toshima City Minami-Otsuka Park 🚊 豊島区立南大塚公園
Cache owner: revue77 🇯🇵

The posted coordinates of this cache take you back in time to a Japanese streetcar that operated from 1949 to 1971. Visitors can experience firsthand the atmosphere of the Shōwa era.

13. GCBDKQJ—! Not for the faint of heart !
Cache owner: Nosaj13 🇺🇸

A major throwback, this cache owner created a cache out of a video cassette container from their non-broadcast job in the 1980s and ‘90s. The log sheet is inside a second container, where SWAG can also be found.

14. GC8Z5MY—Donkey Kong – Gadget Cache
Cache owner: burgo78 🇦🇺

The year is 1981, and Donkey Kong has just been released. To access the log sheet, you must use sticks to move a Mario puck to the top of the box and release it from the game board.

15. GCBF059—Thèmes de pose 2025 : Retour dans le passé 👶 🛴
Cache owner: eureka17 🇫🇷

This back-to-childhood-inspired Letterbox Hybrid cache contains small children’s toys, a logbook, a stamp, and an ink pad. As the cache page states, “something of childhood always remains, always…” and the same is definitely true for us.

What a nostalgia-packed adventure down memory lane! Old-school inspiration and creative design made these caches a true blast from the past.

A huge round of applause to the incredible cache owners who encourage geocachers to spend time in nature every day, and a big thank you to everyone who nominated a geocache for this hiding theme!

Stay tuned for the 2026 Hiding Themes announcement. See you next year!

item.title: Spuren im Sand — Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Mystery
GC4G6AR
by Johannis10
Difficulty:
1.5
Terrain:
1
Location:
Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany
N 51° 50.981′ E 007° 29.337′

Lake Brombach’s shore in Germany is a perfect location for classic beach activities like building sandcastles, stacking stone towers, and drawing smiley faces in the sand. And, of course, it’s also a great spot for geocaching.

Hidden not far from the sand beaches is a geocache masterpiece just waiting for the next geocacher to find.

To find the cache, you have to turn off the lakeside path, as the posted coordinates do not indicate the cache location. To solve this Mystery Cache and locate the final coordinates, geocachers must solve the following simple riddle: Who originally authored the English poem, “Footprints in the Sand?”

A: Margaret Fishback Powers
B: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
C: Carl Olof Rosenius

Depending on the answer chosen, check the cache page for the corresponding reference point.

If you chose the correct answer, follow these directions to the cache:
1. Follow an unpaved forest track about 42 feet (13 meters) north from the bike path
2. Then follow a faint path about 49 feet (15 meters) east


Video by Team_Rhoeny.

To open: Turn the top level counterclockwise until it stops. Pull the screw up until it stops. Do not turn the screw, only pull it up! Turn the top level further.

To close: Turn the lower level past the detent. The screw locks automatically. Turn the upper level clockwise to cover the screw.

The cache owner Johannis10 has some tips to help you avoid injury to yourself and the cache. Please observe the following:

Never insert objects or fingers into cracks or crevices. Proceed slowly and gently, without using force. Do not dig, unscrew anything, lift stones, and supervise children.

Just as the name of the cache indicates, geocachers should leave nothing but footprints in the sand and their username in the logbook, of course. Where will your footprints take you next?

item.title: New for Premium members: All Treasure collections are now active
item.description:
Premium members can now access all available Treasure collections, instead of being limited to three active collections. This makes it easier to collect the Treasure you want without switching between collections.

This update introduces two improvements that players specifically requested:

1. Premium members can set up to five priority collections to collect Treasure from first.
2. Premium members can now view which collections a cache qualifies for on cache pages on Geocaching.com.

Set up to five priority collections

All collections are now active by default for Premium members. Setting “Priority collections” is optional—if you want, you can choose up to five to prioritize. When you log a cache that qualifies for more than one collection, you’ll collect Treasure from the highest-ranked priority collection. If a cache doesn’t match any of your priority collections, but does qualify for another collection that’s not in your priority collections, you’ll still collect Treasure. If you don’t set any priority collections, you’ll continue to collect Treasure from any collection that matches your finds.

Want to save Treasure for a future outing? To collect Treasure only from your priority collections, use the toggle on the right side of the Treasures page.

View Treasure on cache pages on Geocaching.com

Premium members can now see which collections a cache qualifies for directly on the cache page on Geocaching.com. This makes it easier to plan your next outing.

To see what collections a cache qualifies for directly from a cache page, go to a cache page on Geocaching.com and click on “View Treasures” in the list menu on the right hand of the page below the “Log geocache” button. A window will appear that shows which collections the geocache qualifies for.

You can also see which caches match the criteria of a certain Treasures collection by using the filtered search option from the Treasures page in the Geocaching® mobile app or on Geocaching.com.

 

New Treasure collection

We will release one more Treasure collection in 2025. Classic toys will be available starting December 19 at noon UTC. You can collect these Treasures by finding and logging caches with the “Recommended for kids” attribute or attending any Event.

Treasures is an evolving feature for Geocaching.com and the Geocaching® mobile app. We want to hear from you! Share your feedback on Treasures in the web form or in the comments.

item.title: Kijkhut ‘It Gemaaltsje’: Van wol naar weidevogels – Geocache of the week
item.description:
Letterbox Hybrid
GCBAHBK
by NTM27
Difficulty:
2
Terrain:
3.5
Location:
Friesland, Netherlands
N 52° 59.140′ E 005° 31.124′

Some geocaches transport you somewhere new, not just geographically, but into a story shaped by the people who care for a place. Kijkhut ‘It Gemaaltsje’: Van wol naar weidevogels (GCBAHBK) is one of those hides. Blending creativity, community spirit, and nature, this birdwatching hut transforms an old pumping station into a peaceful haven for birdwatchers and geocachers alike.

Visiting this geocache is a seasonal adventure. From March 25 to October 25, the only route to the hut is across the water. A small rowboat named WaarLamke waits at the waypoint, ready to ferry two people over the shallow, calm waters. During the colder months, when meadow birds rest, visitors take a walking path through a local farmer’s field instead.

This is a sensitive, protected place, and respect is essential. As the cache owner, NTM27, reminds us, the cache can thrive only if each visitor treats the environment with care.

 

Once you arrive, you’ll find the cache near the hut. Easy to spot, yet full of creative charm. Its design, a sewing machine inside the box, cleverly nods to the wool art that helped transform It Gemaaltsje, blending story and craftsmanship into one thoughtful hide.

Inside the hut, visitors can enjoy views of the meadows and perhaps catch a glimpse of some birds. It’s a place that invites stillness. A reminder that sometimes, the best finds come when we slow down.

The cache owner, NTM27, shares:

It’s one of my personal favourites as well ☺️ The community is so invested, they really supported a geocache being placed there, which I love too. The foundation was very supportive about me placing it there since not many people know about it, and they love to see more people come and visit it.

Those wishing to learn more or visit responsibly can connect through Instagram at @creativecache. The cache owner emphasizes, “It’s a delicate place, and I want people to visit it the right way so the foundation keeps supporting the cache there.”

Vogelkijkhut ‘It Gemaaltsje’ is more than just a geocache; it is a reflection of creativity, community, and care for the land. It invites geocachers to slow down and experience how art and collaboration can give new meaning to a place once left still.

Once, this small building served as a simple pumping station. When it fell out of use, the people of Sânfurd, a close-knit ‘mienskip’ (community), imagined something more. Their local foundation purchased the structure, and with the help of artist and activist Claudy Jongstra, whose artworks are crafted from local wool, they raised the funds needed to bring a birdwatching hut to life. Her work directly supported the transformation.

With collective effort, the community rebuilt the station into a warm and welcoming hut overlooking the meadows of Greidefûgelgebiet Sânfurd.

Have you ever found a cache that brings art, community, and nature together like this?

item.title: That’s a wrap! GIFF 2025
item.description:
Once again, geocachers came together to celebrate the comedy, drama, and heart-pounding action of geocaching on the big screen.

The Geocaching International Film Festival reminds us that geocaching is about the shared, universal experiences it offers. The stories of geocaching are translatable across the entire global geocaching community, no matter what language you sign the log sheet.

First, let’s do the numbers:

  • There were 61 filmmakers from 21 countries who submitted a film for consideration this year.
  • 20 films from 10 countries were selected as finalists.
  • The final films were viewed at 634 Events across 92 countries, territories, and regions.
  • Event attendees earned 16,335 (and counting!) GIFF 2025 souvenirs.
    • If you attended a GIFF Event, don’t forget to log it!

And now, the moment you’ve all been waiting for… the GIFF Award winners!

The votes have been counted, and we are excited to present this year’s film festival awards: the Signal Award and the People’s Choice Award.

The Signal Award winner is selected by a panel of geocaching community volunteers from around the world. They are asked to consider production quality, content, creativity, and contribution to the global geocaching community.

The People’s Choice Award is chosen by geocachers like you! Nearly 10,000 geocachers voted in this year’s People’s Choice Award for their favorite film.

This year, an interesting phenomenon occurred: volunteers and geocachers chose the same winner.

This year’s Signal Award and People’s Choice Award winner is…

HARD WORK by Harogs Team
(harogs, geocachingclown, and commge)

This Swiss film answered the age-old question: “How do gadget caches work?” They’re powered by tiny workers, of course! These brave employees work day and night to operate the mechanisms that power the most complex caches.

Here’s what volunteers and geocachers said:

“It was a truly unique perspective to how gadget caches work. The sets and the props used in the film were amazing and it had a bit surprising sad ending.”

“Beyond its technical achievements, the content of “HARD WORK” is inspiring. The film shifts the focus from the finder to the creator. It celebrates the often-unseen true “hard work” that goes into designing, building, and maintaining a high-quality, memorable cache. It’s a homage to the cache owners who contribute their passion and time to the community through hiding such caches.”

“Great to see how gadget caches work in the inside ;-)”

“Really great idea, brilliantly executed, even though I’m very sad that the buddy was kidnapped 🙁 I hope that all the hard work will soon be rewarded with a new buddy.”

Honorable mentions

With so many great films this year, we wanted to acknowledge some of the other popular films, as voted by volunteers and geocachers.

  • The BisonBuddy5000 by Skimbosh
  • If You Hide It… by Team Vlogger (geocachingvlogger and Seemyshell)
  • Dogeza by _nokos_ team

Congratulations to the winners, and thank you to all the filmmakers for contributing to an amazing season of GIFF fun. Watch all the GIFF 2025 finalist films on our YouTube channel.

Finally, we’d like to issue a correction and apology to finalist JustCarlo. The GIFF 2025 title page for his film Never A Straight Path listed his location as the USA. This should have been Canada.

Thank yous all around

A huge thanks to all our filmmakers who shared their films with the global community this year. What a fantastic array of voices, ideas, and creativity!

Another big thank you to the Event hosts and behind-the-scenes volunteers who made GIFF 2025 a blockbuster hit! Take a look at some of these GIFF Events from around the world:

    1. More than 110 participants attended GCBBK0A, making it the largest GIFF in Saxony-Anhalt.

    2. Attendees at GCBDPNF rolled out the red carpet for the GIFF Gnomes at their Event in Katsdorf, Austria!

    3. The filmmakers behind the film “HARD WORK” co-hosted GCB3ZMK in Sarnen, Switzerland. This Event featured musical accompaniment by the pianist who composed the film’s score, and participants were able to log their experiences in the original logbook from the film!

    4. Despite the rain, geocachers turned out for GCBDC2V, a soggy GIFF Event in Seattle, USA. As umbrellas and coats dried, attendees enjoyed popcorn, GIFF bingo, and prizes!

    5. Slovenian geocachers congregated in Ljubljana to attend GCBD80Z and its after-party. Organizers conducted a thorough ranked-voting system to determine their own People’s Choice winner.

What’s next?

It’s time once again to press “pause” for another year. The Geocaching International Film Festival will return in 2027.

But it’s never too early to start dusting off those clapboards, brainstorming your film ideas, and practicing your camera work! We can’t wait to see what new stories the community creates next.

item.title: Echoes Beyond the Gate — Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GCAWZTF
by WVangler
Difficulty:
4
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
West Virginia, USA
N 39° 37.722’ W 079° 52.044’

Geocaching has a way of revealing the magical hidden layers of familiar places. Each step feels like the world is offering up a new secret. Often, geocachers report their discoveries of beautiful views or historic landmarks they didn’t know existed.

One such geocache, Echoes Beyond the Gate (GCAWZTF), is cleverly hidden in a unique feature of the West Virginia Botanic Garden, a peaceful sanctuary for wildlife and vibrant blooming flower species.

To get to Ground Zero (GZ), let a trail of mulch guide you through the peaceful botanical garden. As you round an otherwise ordinary corner, a majestic, arching stone-moon-gate welcomes geocachers with a framed path of stepping stones.

As you near the arch, take a closer look and notice the delightful details in the stonework. The left and right sides of the structure feature two designs built into the gate—one in the shape of a heart, while the other illustrates three dots with three lines beneath them, resembling upside-down exclamation marks.

Which compartment hides the prize? The approach to the arch may seem familiar, but the cache owner has a clever twist in store. One of these stones is not like the others and bears the key to the cache. With a sharp eye and some trial and error, one stone slides to the side on rails, and reveals the cavity that holds the esteemed log sheet.

Expect to find a small container; a bison tube is peacefully nestled behind the opening. Sign your name, slide the stone back into place, and leave the secret just as you found it.

Fun fact: The West Virginia Botanic Garden commissioned the custom stone feature to make a big splash at the 2025 GeoWoodstock. Now, that’s dedication to geocaching!

What’s your favorite geocache? Let us know in the comments.
